attributes.provenance: discovered live during the 2026-08-31 symbol-adoption pass (work_claim.symbol-adoption.20260831.v1): renaming 4 of the 24 adopted symbols (fn_80089350, fn_80091AC0, fn_800920E0, pbSetDODrawRegs) broke `python memory_graph/gdlmem.py build` project-wide with 'record references unknown entity function:fn_80089350' immediately afterward, because pre-existing accepted attempt records anchored their `function` field to the OLD fn_ name.
attributes.scope: the memory_graph tooling (memory_graph/core.py _autoresolve_entity / _entity_id), any project session; applies to every future symbol-rename campaign, not just fn_* placeholder adoption

subject: project:gdl
value: `function:<name>` entity references (used by every attempt record's required `function` field, and by claim `subject`/`object` fields that use the same form) resolve LIVE against the CURRENT config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt via memory_graph/core.py's `_autoresolve_entity` (raw_name lookup in the imported binary_symbol table) -- there is no rename-tracking or alias layer. Renaming a function's symbols.txt entry therefore silently ORPHANS every existing attempt/claim record whose `function`/`subject` field used the OLD name: the very next `gdlmem.py build`/`ensure`/`context`/any-command-that-rebuilds fails hard with 'record references unknown entity ...' and blocks ALL graph queries project-wide (not just for the renamed symbol) until repaired, because attempt-record validation runs at INSERT time for every record file on disk -- superseding a record with a new `supersedes`-pointing v2 does NOT exempt the OLD v1 file from this validation; it still gets loaded and still fails. Verified: 4 records broke the graph in the 2026-08-31 pass (attempt.fn-80089350-portable-closure.20260829.v1, attempt.parked.fn_80091ac0.20260829.v1, attempt.parked.fn_800920e0.20260829.v1, attempt.parked.pbsetdodrawregs.20260829.v1); `gdlmem.py build` failed fast on the first one encountered, hiding the other three until each was fixed in turn. Fix procedure (verified this pass): before or immediately after any symbols.txt rename, grep memory_graph/records/ (and memory_graph/inbox/) for the OLD name; for every hit whose field is literally `"function": "function:<OLD_NAME>"` (not just a prose mention elsewhere in the record), edit that field in place to `"function:<NEW_NAME>"` -- this is a narrow POINTER repair (the anchored finding/content is unchanged, only the reference that keeps it discoverable), not a content supersession, and does not need a new record version. Then re-run `gdlmem.py build` to confirm the graph resolves cleanly, and confirm with `gdlmem.py context <NEW_NAME>` that the historical record surfaces correctly. Recommendation for the tool: `gdlmem.py` should offer a `rename-symbol <old> <new>` helper that does the symbols.txt edit, the source-wide identifier rename, AND this record-pointer repair as one atomic, gated operation -- doing it by hand is exactly how this class of bug gets missed.
